title: Code format scanner
statement: For a code format $F$, the scanner takes a bit string, decodes it as a pair of a length code and a remainder, and lets $n$ be the natural number represented by the length code. It returns no result unless that code is exactly the bit representation of $n$ and the remainder has at least $g(n+1)$ bits, where $g$ is the format’s guard constant. Otherwise it removes the unary encoding of a state index in the range of $n+1$ states, then removes the encoded transition table; it succeeds with the remaining suffix precisely when every bit in that suffix is $1$.
hypotheses_covered: Input is a finite bit string
caveat: The supplied statement does not include definitions of the pair decoder, natural-number bit representation, unary-prefix skipper, or table skipper, so their precise parsing conventions cannot be fully stated.
